content: Topic: Arrays. Concept: A contiguous block of memory storing elements of the same type under a single identifier.. Intuition: Like a row of numbered lockers next to each other where you can access any locker instantly using its index.
Topic: Arrays complexities. Time Complexity: O(N) linear, O(log N) if sorted binary. Space Complexity: N/A.
Topic: Arrays common mistakes & pitfalls: Off-by-one errors (accessing index len(arr) instead of len(arr)-1). Iterating and modifying size dynamically without tracking indices.
Topic: Arrays edge cases: Empty array. Array with 1 element. Duplicate values. Negative indices in python.

Topic: Arrays interview tips: Mention contiguous memory cache locality. If array is sorted, think of Binary Search or Two Pointers.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 1: Two Sum, LeetCode 26: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array.

Topic: Strings. Concept: A sequence of characters, often implemented as an array of characters under the hood.. Intuition: Like a train where each car holds a single letter. Immutable in languages like Java/Python, mutable in C++.
Topic: Strings complexities. Time Complexity: O(N) linear, KMP is O(N+M). Space Complexity: N/A.
Topic: Strings common mistakes & pitfalls: Creating strings inside loops (leading to O(N^2) time due to copies in immutable structures). Ignoring case sensitivity or whitespace.
Topic: Strings edge cases: Empty string (""). String with spaces only. Anagrams/Palindromes of odd/even length.

Topic: Strings interview tips: If dealing with character counts or anagrams, use an array of size 26 or 128 as a lightweight frequency map.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 344: Reverse String, LeetCode 242: Valid Anagram.

Topic: Hash Maps. Concept: A data structure that maps keys to values using a hashing function for near-instant access.. Intuition: Like a post office where your name hashes to a specific PO box index where your mail is kept.
Topic: Hash Maps complexities. Time Complexity: N/A. Space Complexity: N/A.
Topic: Hash Maps common mistakes & pitfalls: Forgetting key collision resolution (Chaining vs Open Addressing). Modifying key objects while they are inside the map.
Topic: Hash Maps edge cases: Hash key collisions. Empty map checks. Resizing threshold triggers.

Topic: Hash Maps interview tips: Always discuss load factor and how collision resolution works (e.g. linked list chaining or linear probing).. Practice Problems: LeetCode 136: Single Number, LeetCode 387: First Unique Character in a String.

Topic: Stack. Concept: A Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) linear data structure where elements are inserted and removed from the same end.. Intuition: Like a stack of dinner plates; you can only place a new plate on the top, and you must take the top plate off first.
Topic: Stack complexities. Time Complexity: O(N). Space Complexity: N/A.
Topic: Stack common mistakes & pitfalls: Calling pop() or peek() on an empty stack (Stack Underflow). Recursion limit stack overflow during depth first searches.
Topic: Stack edge cases: Empty stack. Stack with one element. Capacity limit overflow (fixed-size stacks).

Topic: Stack interview tips: Use stacks for backtracking, balanced parentheses, prefix/postfix expressions, and simulating recursion.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 20: Valid Parentheses, LeetCode 155: Min Stack.

Topic: Queue. Concept: A First-In, First-Out (FIFO) linear data structure where elements are inserted at the rear (enqueue) and removed from the front (dequeue).. Intuition: Like a line at a grocery store checkout; the first person who gets in line is served first.
Topic: Queue complexities. Time Complexity: N/A. Space Complexity: N/A.

Topic: Queue common mistakes & pitfalls: Using a standard list for queues in Python (leads to O(N) dequeue because elements shift). Use collections.deque!. Forgetting to update rear/front pointers in custom array circular queues.
Topic: Queue edge cases: Empty queue. Circular buffer overflow. Queue with 1 item.

Topic: Queue interview tips: Used in Breadth-First Search (BFS), task scheduling, buffers, and message queues.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 225: Implement Stack using Queues, LeetCode 933: Number of Recent Calls.

Topic: Linked List. Concept: A linear collection of data elements called nodes, where each node points to the next node in sequence.. Intuition: Like a scavenger hunt; you start at the first clue, and each clue tells you where to find the next clue.
Topic: Linked List complexities. Time Complexity: O(N). Space Complexity: N/A.
Topic: Linked List common mistakes & pitfalls: Losing node pointers during insertion/deletion, causing list disconnection. Dereferencing null pointer (`None.next`).
Topic: Linked List edge cases: List is empty (head is Null). Single element list. Cycles/loops in list. Deleting head node.

Topic: Linked List interview tips: Use a 'Dummy Node' at the head to simplify node additions/deletions. Think of Two Pointers (Slow/Fast) to find cycles or midpoints.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 206: Reverse Linked List, LeetCode 141: Linked List Cycle.

Topic: Trees. Concept: A hierarchical data structure consisting of nodes connected by edges, with a single node designated as root.. Intuition: Like a corporate hierarchy tree or folder directories on your computer storage.
Topic: Trees complexities. Time Complexity: N/A. Space Complexity: N/A.
Topic: Trees common mistakes & pitfalls: Treating trees as lists or graphs (forgetting trees have no cycles and exactly one parent). Forgetting leaf node termination base case in recursion.
Topic: Trees edge cases: Empty tree (root is Null). Skewed tree (essentially a linked list, degrading operations to O(N)). Tree with only root node.

Topic: Trees interview tips: Master Preorder, Inorder, and Postorder traversals. Inorder traversal of a BST visits nodes in sorted order.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 104: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree, LeetCode 94: Binary Tree Inorder Traversal.

Topic: BST. Concept: A Binary Search Tree (BST) is a binary tree where left child nodes are smaller than parent, and right child nodes are larger.. Intuition: Allows divide-and-conquer searching; at each node, we discard half the remaining possibilities.
Topic: BST complexities. Time Complexity: O(log N) average, O(N) worst case. Space Complexity: N/A.

Topic: BST common mistakes & pitfalls: Assuming a binary tree is a BST without verifying all left descendants are smaller than parent (not just immediate left child). Allowing tree to degrade into skewed linked list (Operations become O(N)).
Topic: BST edge cases: Empty BST. Inserting duplicate values. Skewed tree (elements inserted in sorted order).

Topic: BST interview tips: Inorder traversal visits elements in ascending order. Remember that deletion has three cases: leaf, single child, and double children (replace with successor).. Practice Problems: LeetCode 700: Search in a Binary Search Tree, LeetCode 98: Validate Binary Search Tree.

Topic: AVL. Concept: A self-balancing Binary Search Tree where the heights of the left and right subtrees of any node differ by at most one.. Intuition: Like a tree that auto-rotates itself whenever it gets too heavy on one side to keep tree depth balanced.
Topic: AVL complexities. Time Complexity: O(log N) guaranteed. Space Complexity: N/A.
Topic: AVL common mistakes & pitfalls: Forgetting to update node heights during rotations. Incorrectly determining rotation type (e.g. confusing LR with LL).
Topic: AVL edge cases: Empty tree. Single element tree. Deep updates that trigger cascading rotations up to the root.

Topic: AVL interview tips: Mention that AVL trees are more rigidly balanced than Red-Black trees, making lookups faster but insertions/deletions slightly more rotation-intensive.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 108: Convert Sorted Array to Binary Search Tree (leads to balanced tree).

Topic: Heap. Concept: A complete binary tree that satisfies the heap property: Max-Heap (parent node is larger than children) or Min-Heap (parent is smaller).. Intuition: Like a leaderboard; the highest (or lowest) value is always at the top, and updating it takes logarithmic time.
Topic: Heap complexities. Time Complexity: N/A. Space Complexity: N/A.

Topic: Heap common mistakes & pitfalls: Using a sorted list instead of a heap (O(N) insert instead of O(log N)). Attempting to index arbitrary elements in O(1) in a heap (heaps only guarantee top element access in O(1)).
Topic: Heap edge cases: Empty heap. Single element heap. Extracting from heap of size 1.

Topic: Heap interview tips: Heaps are excellent for 'K-way merge', finding 'K-th largest/smallest elements', and scheduling algorithms.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 215: Kth Largest Element in an Array, LeetCode 703: Kth Largest Element in a Stream.

Topic: Trie. Concept: An information retrieval tree (prefix tree) used to store associative arrays where keys are usually strings.. Intuition: Like search autocomplete; as you type letters, you traverse down a character path representing words.
Topic: Trie complexities. Time Complexity: O(L). Space Complexity: N/A.

Topic: Trie common mistakes & pitfalls: Excessive memory consumption (creating 26-pointer arrays for empty nodes). Optimize with hashmap children!. Forgetting to mark `isWord=True` on completed words.
Topic: Trie edge cases: Empty string insertion. Searching for prefix vs full word. Duplicate word insertion.

Topic: Trie interview tips: Great for auto-complete, spelling checkers, IP routing lookups, and prefix matches.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 208: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree), LeetCode 211: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure.

Topic: Graphs. Concept: A collection of vertices (nodes) and edges connecting pairs of vertices.. Intuition: Like a social network where people are nodes and friendships are edges, or city maps with highways.
Topic: Graphs complexities. Time Complexity: N/A. Space Complexity: N/A.
Topic: Graphs common mistakes & pitfalls: Infinite loops in traversal due to cycles (Must track visited nodes using a set!). Confusing directed vs undirected graph structures.
Topic: Graphs edge cases: Disconnected components. Cycles. Self-loops. Empty graph.

Topic: Graphs interview tips: Use BFS for shortest paths in unweighted graphs. Use DFS for topological sorting and cycle detection.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 200: Number of Islands, LeetCode 207: Course Schedule.

Topic: Union Find. Concept: A disjoint-set data structure that tracks partition of elements into mutually joint sets, supporting Union and Find operations.. Intuition: Like tracking who belongs to which social club, allowing you to merge clubs or check if two people belong to the same club instantly.
Topic: Union Find complexities. Time Complexity: N/A. Space Complexity: N/A.
Topic: Union Find common mistakes & pitfalls: Forgetting path compression in `find()` (degrades Find performance from O(alpha(N)) to O(N)). Merging sets without updates to Rank/Size.
Topic: Union Find edge cases: Single element queries. Union of elements already in the same set. Skewed trees of set parents.

Topic: Union Find interview tips: Used in Kruskal's MST algorithm, cycle detection in undirected graphs, and social connection groups.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 547: Number of Provinces, LeetCode 684: Redundant Connection.

Topic: Binary Search. Concept: An algorithm to search sorted arrays by repeatedly dividing search intervals in halves.. Intuition: If your target is larger than midpoint, search only the right side; else, search the left side.
Topic: Binary Search complexities. Time Complexity: O(log N). Space Complexity: O(1) iterative.

Topic: Binary Search common mistakes & pitfalls: Using `(L+R) // 2` which causes integer overflow in languages with fixed integer sizes. Use `L + (R-L) // 2`. Incorrect boundary updates (`L = Mid` or `R = Mid`, causing infinite loops).
Topic: Binary Search edge cases: Array of size 1. Target is not present. Duplicates in search range.

Topic: Binary Search interview tips: Always check if inputs are sorted. Remember binary search can also run on values (binary search on answer).. Practice Problems: LeetCode 704: Binary Search, LeetCode 34: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array.

Topic: Sliding Window. Concept: A technique that performs operations on a specific window size of a sequence, shifting the window right.. Intuition: Like a security camera frame moving across a street; instead of recalculating the whole frame, you add elements entering from the right and subtract elements leaving from the left.

Topic: Sliding Window complexities. Time Complexity: O(N) (each element processed at most twice: once entering, once leaving). Space Complexity: O(1) if tracking counts, O(K) if storing window elements.
Topic: Sliding Window common mistakes & pitfalls: Incorrect window boundary updates. Updating metrics before resizing the window pointers.
Topic: Sliding Window edge cases: Window size larger than array length. Empty array. Window size is 1.

Topic: Sliding Window interview tips: Useful for subarray or substring queries matching constraint boundaries (e.g. longest substring, minimum sum subarray).. Practice Problems: LeetCode 3: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters, LeetCode 209: Minimum Size Subarray Sum.

Topic: Two Pointers. Concept: A technique using two index pointers to traverse a collection, often moving from ends toward center or in different directions.. Intuition: Like two hikers starting from opposite ends of a bridge and walking toward each other until they meet.
Topic: Two Pointers complexities. Time Complexity: O(N). Space Complexity: O(1).
Topic: Two Pointers common mistakes & pitfalls: Pointers crossing each other and looping infinitely. Index out of bounds on array edges.
Topic: Two Pointers edge cases: Array size < 2. Target sum is impossible. Array with negative numbers.

Topic: Two Pointers interview tips: If array is sorted, Two Pointers can find target sums in linear time. Also useful for reversing sequences or in-place modifications.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 167: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted, LeetCode 15: 3Sum.

Topic: Prefix Sum. Concept: A preprocessing technique where an array is converted into a cumulative sum array, allowing constant time range sum queries.. Intuition: Instead of recounting the cash in your wallet every time someone asks, you keep a running tally of how much you added at each step.
Topic: Prefix Sum complexities. Time Complexity: N/A. Space Complexity: O(N) (or O(1) if modified in-place).

Topic: Prefix Sum common mistakes & pitfalls: Off-by-one errors (failing to insert a 0 at index 0 of prefix array, which complicates query calculations starting from index 0). Overwriting values incorrectly in mutable scenarios.
Topic: Prefix Sum edge cases: Empty array. Queries targeting index 0. Array with negative numbers.

Topic: Prefix Sum interview tips: Perfect for range sum queries. Also works for 2D grids (2D prefix sums).. Practice Problems: LeetCode 303: Range Sum Query - Immutable, LeetCode 560: Subarray Sum Equals K.

Topic: Greedy. Concept: An algorithmic paradigm that makes the locally optimal choice at each step with the hope of finding a global optimum.. Intuition: Taking the highest value coin available at each step to change money, which works for standard currencies but not all custom coin sets.
Topic: Greedy complexities. Time Complexity: O(N log N) if sorting is required, O(N) otherwise. Space Complexity: O(1) or O(N) if tracking allocations.

Topic: Greedy common mistakes & pitfalls: Assuming greedy choices lead to globally optimal solutions (greedy fails on fractional knapsack or general graph traversals without validation). Failing to prove greedy choice property correctness.
Topic: Greedy edge cases: Empty inputs. Negative values in optimization sets. Ties in optimal local decisions.

Topic: Greedy interview tips: Prove your greedy approach by induction or contradiction. If sorting elements by a ratio or size works, it's likely greedy.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 55: Jump Game, LeetCode 435: Non-overlapping Intervals.

Topic: Dynamic Programming. Concept: An algorithmic technique that solves complex problems by breaking them into overlapping subproblems, solving each subproblem once, and storing solutions.. Intuition: If I ask you what 1+1+1+1+1 is, you count to 5. If I add another '+1', you remember the '5' and add 1 to get 6. You didn't recount from scratch!
Topic: Dynamic Programming complexities. Time Complexity: O(Number of States * Transition Time). Space Complexity: O(Number of States) (can often be optimized to O(1) space).

Topic: Dynamic Programming common mistakes & pitfalls: Recalculating subproblems without storing values (no memoization/tabulation, leading to exponential O(2^N) time). Incorrect state transition relations.
Topic: Dynamic Programming edge cases: Base cases (N=0, N=1). Negative values in state tables. Memory limits in large state dimensions.

Topic: Dynamic Programming interview tips: Identify if the problem has 'Overlapping Subproblems' and 'Optimal Substructure'. Define the DP state table and transitions clearly.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 70: Climbing Stairs, LeetCode 322: Coin Change.

Topic: Recursion. Concept: A programming method where a function calls itself directly or indirectly to solve smaller instances of the same problem.. Intuition: Like Russian nesting dolls; you open a doll to find a smaller doll inside, until you reach the smallest doll (base case) and stop.
Topic: Recursion complexities. Time Complexity: O(Branches^Depth). Space Complexity: O(Depth) due to recursive call stack memory allocation.
Topic: Recursion common mistakes & pitfalls: Forgetting the base case, causing infinite loops and Stack Overflow errors. Failing to make progress toward base case in recursive parameters.
Topic: Recursion edge cases: Inputs that trigger base case immediately. Recursive depth limits exceeded (Python default recursion limit is 1000).

Topic: Recursion interview tips: Always identify the base case first. Draw the recursion tree to visualize call paths and complexity.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 509: Fibonacci Number, LeetCode 206: Reverse Linked List (Recursive).

Topic: Backtracking. Concept: A systematic method for searching all (or some) solutions to a problem, which builds candidates and abandons a candidate ('backtracks') as soon as it cannot lead to a valid solution.. Intuition: Like walking through a maze; when you hit a dead end, you walk back to the last intersection and try a different path.
Topic: Backtracking complexities. Time Complexity: O(N!) or O(2^N) in worst cases. Space Complexity: O(N) recursion stack.

Topic: Backtracking common mistakes & pitfalls: Forgetting to undo the choice/state change after recursive call (failing to restore variables to their original state). Failing to prune branches, leading to complete brute force search.
Topic: Backtracking edge cases: Target is reached immediately. Empty input sets. No valid solutions exist.

Topic: Backtracking interview tips: Write down the state template: 1. Base Case (check solution), 2. Loop choices, 3. Make Choice, 4. Recurse, 5. Undo Choice.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 46: Permutations, LeetCode 78: Subsets.

Topic: Bit Manipulation. Concept: An algorithmic technique that performs logical operations directly on the binary representation of integers.. Intuition: Directly flipping light switches (bits) on a control board instead of using complex decimal arithmetic operations.
Topic: Bit Manipulation complexities. Time Complexity: O(1) constant time hardware operations. Space Complexity: O(1).

Topic: Bit Manipulation common mistakes & pitfalls: Operator precedence errors (e.g. `x & 1 == 0` evaluates as `x & (1 == 0)` due to high precedence of comparison). Use parentheses: `(x & 1) == 0`. Forgetting integer bit limits (32-bit vs 64-bit systems).
Topic: Bit Manipulation edge cases: Zero values. Negative numbers (Two's complement representation). Overflow values.

Topic: Bit Manipulation interview tips: XOR property: `a ^ a = 0` and `a ^ 0 = a`. Bit shifts: `x << 1` multiplies by 2, `x >> 1` divides by 2.. Practice Problems: LeetCode 191: Number of 1 Bits, LeetCode 136: Single Number.
